mssrinivas.name: mssrinivas/PayPerView
mssrinivas.description: This project introduces a new concept called "Pay Per View" using the concept of micropayments. The idea is about instead of forcing a user to take a complete subscription of organization's or an application's premium services where user is only interested in subset of the services. Instead user will be charged only for the services he/she wants to consume.  Extension to the current applications Earlier micro payments were not a rage because of transaction cost attached to it, which affets the organizations revenue or an individual. But after the introduction of Online wallet and crypto currency the concept of micropayments has become easy.

mssrinivas.name: mssrinivas/Distributed-File-Storage
mssrinivas.description: This project provides a detailed explanation of the data replication part in the Distributed File Storage System. In a distributed system, data replication ensures reliability and availability among nodes: if one or more servers fail, the system can still function properly even though the node which contains the write is not available. The performance of the system can also be improved due to lower access time and higher scalability; we can reduce response time as the data can be acquired locally, and the system can scale better as requests can be serviced by multiple servers instead of one.

mssrinivas.name: mssrinivas/Slack-Clone
mssrinivas.description: The developed aims to achieve the following objectives:  Development of a messaging application which allows users to post fast, durable messages to other users and groups.  Integration of the developed messaging application with a Buffer space (Kafka message Queue) that increases the durability of the stored messages in cases of complete memory consumption and network partition.  Integrating a durable messaging system which allows the separation of concerns between scaling and database (Database independent message queueing).  Kafka ensures message delivery at least once (Delivery guarantee). Message offsets that help consumers (The Backend Spring Boot Application here) track the point till which messages have been consumed from the Kafka queue.   Deployment of the messaging application with the Kafka broker to the cloud (AWS) where replicated instances are maintained which are served with Elastic Load Balancers to forward requests fairly.

MO-Elmu.description: This was the final big assignment in Stanford CS110. The objective is to harness the power of multiprocessing, networking, threads, concurrency, distributed computing, the Stanford "myth" computer cluster, and the shared AFS file system to build a fully operational MapReduce framework.

MO-Elmu.name: MO-Elmu/Stanford-Shell_stsh

MO-Elmu.name: MO-Elmu/Heap-Allocator
MO-Elmu.description: The Stanford CS107 assignment was to design and implement an allocator that implements malloc, realloc, and free. The allocator obtains a large contiguous segment from the OS and parcels out this segment to service dynamic allocation requests.

MO-Elmu.name: MO-Elmu/RSS-News-Feed-Aggregation
MO-Elmu.description: RSS news feeds are XML documents with information about online news articles. This Stanford CS110 assignment is about building an index of information similar to that held by news.google.com.

MO-Elmu.name: MO-Elmu/HTTP-Web-Proxy-and-Cache
MO-Elmu.description: As part of the Stanford CS110, I was asked to implement a multithreaded HTTP proxy and cache.  HTTP proxy intercepts each and every HTTP request and (generally) forwards it on the intended recipient.  The servers direct their HTTP responses back to the proxy, which in turn passes them on to the client.  This implementation doesn't account for HTTPS only HTTP.

MO-Elmu.name: MO-Elmu/RSS-News-Aggregator_Take-II
MO-Elmu.description: In the last multi-threaded RSS News Feed Aggregator I used as many threads as needed to concurrently download news articles from around the globe and build a news.google.com-like search index. This time I am going to revisit the aggregate executable but I am going to use and rely on a limited number of threads employing the notion of Thread Pool.

MO-Elmu.name: MO-Elmu/Simple-Sudoku
MO-Elmu.description: Our approach will concentrate on OOP and API design. There are many ways to solve Sudoku. We will use an approach which is a sort of OOP interpretation of classic recursive backtracking search.

MO-Elmu.name: MO-Elmu/Mobile-Draw_Android
MO-Elmu.description: It is a very limited paint-like drawing App for Android. This simple application only allows the user to draw rectangles and ovals. The README gives more details.

MO-Elmu.name: MO-Elmu/Bank-Simulation_Threads1
MO-Elmu.description: This code will simulate a bank. Our bank will track the balances in twenty different accounts. When the program begins, each of the accounts contains $1000. The program will process a list of transactions which transfer money between the accounts. Once all transactions have been processed the program will go through and for each account it will print both the account’s final balance and the number of transactions (deposits and withdrawals) which occurred on that account.

maringantis.name: maringantis/Proxy-Cache-Server
maringantis.description: Cache web proxy server is an intermediate server between the client and the main server. The proxy server is used to reduce the bandwidth, latency and the server load. The cache web proxy server caches the client’s requests to the server. Each client request goes through the proxy server. The cache web proxy server responds to the client with the requested information if the files exist. If the cache web proxy doesn’t host the requested information, it talks to the server and fetches the requested information. The subsequent requests to that file will be handled by the cache web proxy server instead of the main server hosting the files. The cache web proxy server fetches the files from the main server until its buffer runs out. The server then deletes the files to make space for the new files.

maringantis.name: maringantis/UDP-Socket-Throughput
maringantis.description: The server should take 3 command line arguments: the port number from which it reads requests, the message size in bytes, and the sleep time in milliseconds. The server will read a message of the specified size from a client. After that, it will sleep for the specified amount of time (to simulate injected network latency) and then send an acknowledgment for the received message back to the client. Each client message will have a unique sequence number, which is included in the ack sent by the server. The server repeats this for 30 messages and then exit. The client will take 3 command line arguments: the IP address (or the host name) and port number of the server, and the message size in bytes. The client will write a message of the specified size to the server and wait for the ack from the server. The client will repeat this 30 times and keep track of the total amount of time spent on sending all the messages and receiving all the acks. It computes the throughput by: 30 * message_size_in_bytes / total_time_in_seconds and print the throughput value. After that, the client should exit.

maringantis.name: maringantis/Emulation-of-CPU
maringantis.description: The project consisted of many phases.In this project we had to code the functionalities and the model of CPU with all its vital components. We had created our own assembly rules and code for our CPU. We did code the entire project in "C".  The initial phase consisted of created all the registers, ALU ,control unit and all the flags required. Later we designed the arithmetic unit and the logic. Later the controls and the loop we designed which work for the assembly function we wrote.By the end of all phase the CPU could compute basic functionalities.

maringantis.name: maringantis/Distributed-client-server-model
maringantis.description: The project involves the primitives of developing a distributed system.The distributed system we developed had two servers and a client. The model had to compute and calculate the arithmetic. The first server has few operators and the second system other operations. If the client requested the arithmetic involving the operator from the first client then the response is directed to the client.If the arithmetic involves the operation from the second server then the operation is first checked in the initial server then checks in the next server.If the operation is found it computes the calculation and returns the value to the first server, then this server returns the required response to the client. If the requested operation is not found in any server then it prompts for any other operation.

mharish2797.name: mharish2797/DNN-Text-Classifiers
mharish2797.description: After the advent of convolutional and recurrent neural networks, the content based intelligent classification is being given high priority. But the biased feature learning by recurrent networks and window restricted feature learning by convolutional networks restrict the performance of these networks.   In this project, three variants of deep learning based text classification system for combining the convolutional and recurrent networks in parallel manner that overcomes their individual limitations is proposed. We also propose a novel activation function Inverse Exponential Linear Unit (IELU) that allows the network to learn more features in comparison with traditional activation functions like Rectified Linear unit and Exponential Linear unit.   The throughput of the system is analysed by considering a variety of datasets and performance metrics into consideration. It has been inferred that all the three parallel architectures have higher performance when compared with the existing classification systems. Also, our IELU performs better than the widely used activation functions in text classification application.

mahnooriftikharrr.name: mahnooriftikharrr/Photo-Editor
mahnooriftikharrr.description: The Image Modification Program is a Java-based application that modifies PPM image files allowing users to apply image transformations, such as negation, quantization, grayscale conversion, and horizontal flipping.

mahnooriftikharrr.name: mahnooriftikharrr/Elevation-Optimized-Pathfinding
mahnooriftikharrr.description: This project demonstrates the use of a greedy algorithm to solve the problem of finding optimal paths through a mountain range, coded in Java.

mahnooriftikharrr.name: mahnooriftikharrr/NY-Times-Spellingbee-Solver
mahnooriftikharrr.description: The Newyork Times Spelling Bee Solver is a Java-based application that helps users solve the popular Spelling Bee puzzle. Users can input a set of 7 letters, and the program will find all valid words from a dictionary that meet the puzzle's rules. The application features a graphical user interface (GUI) for an interactive experience.

mahnooriftikharrr.name: mahnooriftikharrr/Two-Step
mahnooriftikharrr.description: TwoStep is an adaptive music therapy platform for gait rehabilitation in Parkinson’s and other motor disorders. It captures a patient’s step rhythm, compares it to therapeutic targets, and uses the Suno API to generate music that adapts tempo and style in real time, guiding movement and reinforcing motor learning.

mahnooriftikharrr.name: mahnooriftikharrr/Flood-Fill-Algorithm
mahnooriftikharrr.description: Flood Fill  is an image-processing algorithm that colors all connected pixels of similar color starting from a given seed point, the same concept used in tools like the Paint Bucket in Photoshop or MS Paint.

mahnooriftikharrr.name: mahnooriftikharrr/Stack-Based-Expression-Parser
mahnooriftikharrr.description: This project implements a stack-based algorithm to evaluate infix arithmetic expressions. The program demonstrates the use of data structures, operator precedence, and algorithmic parsing to compute results from mathematical expressions mimicking how interpreters and compilers handle syntax evaluation.

mahnooriftikharrr.name: mahnooriftikharrr/LinkedList-Labyrinth
mahnooriftikharrr.description: A Java-based exploration project where I navigated and escaped a maze built entirely from linked memory structures. Each maze cell was a node connected by directional pointers (north, south, east, west).

mahnooriftikharrr.name: mahnooriftikharrr/Arbitrary-Precision-Arithmetic
mahnooriftikharrr.description: Understanding of ArrayLists, algorithm design, and object-oriented programming through implementation of large integer arithmetic using ArrayList without relying on Java’s built-in BigInteger.

mahnooriftikharrr.name: mahnooriftikharrr/SodukoSolver
mahnooriftikharrr.description: A Java-based algorithmic project that demonstrates the power of recursion, backtracking, and constraint satisfaction to solve any valid 9x9 Sudoku puzzle.

mahnooriftikharrr.name: mahnooriftikharrr/ShapeEngine
mahnooriftikharrr.description: This project showcases object-oriented programming (OOP) principles through the design of a 2D game engine component that models, renders, and interacts with geometric shapes like rectangles and ellipses.

mahnooriftikharrr.name: mahnooriftikharrr/Navigator
mahnooriftikharrr.description: Navigator is a a Java console application that locates the nearest point of interest like a restaurant, park, or concert hall, based on user input for location and keywords. Think of it as a mini Google Maps built entirely in core Java using object-oriented programming and the Haversine distance formula.

mohito83.name: mohito83/socket-programming
mohito83.description: Simulation of a logistic system, where the communication between central warehouse and four outlets is established over TCP and UDP sockets. This project has two phases: Phase1 is inventory reporting where the communication between the warehouse and outlets takes place over the TCP sockets. Phase2 is stock replenishment for which the communications between the outlets and warehouse takes place over UDP sockets.  This project was developed using C language over UNIX/Solaris platform

mohito83.name: mohito83/socket-programming1
mohito83.description: Simulation of various queue systems and comparison of their system parameters with theoretical results. This project has 3 phases: Phase1 simulates M/M/1 and M/M/N/K queues for different arrival and service rates, and different sample sizes. Phase2 simulates M/M/1 queues with feedback for different arrival and service rates, and feedback probability. Phase3 simulates M/G/1 FIFO queues for different sample size and seeds for generating random variables.  This project was developed using C++ language over UNIX/Solaris platform.

mohito83.name: mohito83/EE597-Anypath
mohito83.description: Comparison between the Shortest Single Path (Djikstra's) routing and Any Path routing schemes in a wireless network, using Matlab simulation models. The simulation is performed for different network topologies and channel model parameters. And from simulation results it is inferred for IEEE802.11 networks the Any Path routing performs significantly better than Djikstra's routing.

mohito83.name: mohito83/EE597-DCF
mohito83.description: Study of saturation throughput in an IEEE802.11 network using DCF by using NS-2 simulation models. The simulation result analyze the throughput region first for increasing number of nodes and second by fixing the number of nodes and increasing the data rate.

mohito83.name: mohito83/facebook-mashup
mohito83.description: Development of IMDB and Facebook mashup web application, which allow users to search their favorite movie/tv show/video game on IMDB.com and enable them to post it on their Facebook account using a web browser. The same functionality is ported to mobile devices by developing an Android mobile application.  The Phase 1 of project is developed using PHP, Java servlet, Javascript, HTML, CSS, JSON, XML and AJAX technologies. And is deployed on a Apache-Tomcat setup. Phase 2 is developed using Android
